summary: Tested Lex global research admin endpoints, the source-change review queue, the AI discovery switch, 4 paid national chat calls (DE, PL, US-Texas, GB) and the ResearchHealthCard in admin Settings. Backend: 12 of 13 pass. The one failure is a malformed change id returning 500. All 4 chat checks pass: DE cites BGB §573, §573c and §574 from gesetze-im-internet.de. PL says '21 dni' citing art. 264 (api.sejm.gov.pl ...#art-264). US-Texas uses no U.S. Code or govinfo citation, and the Texas site results are labelled 'currency and in-force status NOT confirmed'. The GB legislation.gov.uk ERA 1996 sources are still present. Frontend: the card renders, Details opens the table, coverage list, change rows and AI switch, and the switch turns off and back on. A UI-inserted change was marked 'no guidance affected' and disappeared. LawMonitoringCard still shows 'OFF · 0 of 17' and was not touched. The existing suite test_global_research.py is now flaky: 39 of 40 passed, and the PL link test fails about 2 times in 3 on a cold cache.

minor.issue: An id that is not valid (e.g. 'not-an-id') returns 500: ObjectId(cid) raises bson.errors.InvalidId (seen in backend.err.log). Wrap it in try/except and return 404 (or 400).

Downloads are not shared. Each Polish article ref (KP 264/30/45/36) downloads and parses the whole multi-MB Kodeks pracy PDF on its own, and REF_WAIT is 2.5s with a semaphore of 3. On a cold cache only 2 of the 4 provisions come back in time. test_global_research.py::test_each_retrieved_provision_has_its_own_link_so_none_is_dropped fails about 2 times in 3 when run alone with AIA_NO_PAID=1. Fix: keep one shared download per law in _pl_doc (an in-flight future for pl-doc:{law}). The live server is fine while the Mongo legal_source_records cache is warm.

The Texas site results have claim_check='reference_found_in_source' while the title says 'no specific provision identified ... NOT confirmed'. The two signals contradict each other, so consider claim_check='unchecked' for site-search extracts. They are also tagged source='official' even though Lex could not open the page.

backend.err.log shows 2 earlier 'Tavily 432: exceeds your plan's set usage limit' entries from before this run. Tavily worked during this run (Texas search returned results), but the plan limit is close.

issues: Card title 'Lex legal research' is white and plain. The cards next to it (e.g. 'Fair use & spending') use the gold heading style.
Coverage names start with a lowercase article ('the United Kingdom', 'the UAE'). This looks odd in a list.
No loading or error state: the card returns null if the health call fails, so an admin gets no clue why it is missing. The review and toggle actions show no error feedback.

action_items: Return 404/400 instead of 500 for a malformed ObjectId in POST /api/admin/lex-research/source-changes/{cid}/review

Share one in-flight PDF download per law in national_law._pl_doc so a cold PL question returns all mapped provisions; this also fixes the flaky test_each_retrieved_provision_has_its_own_link_so_none_is_dropped
Optional: set claim_check to 'unchecked' for site-search (Tavily) extracts, to match the 'not confirmed' label
Optional: ResearchHealthCard design polish (gold heading, plural wording, error state)
critical_code_review_comments: research_admin.review: ObjectId(cid) is not validated, so a bad id gives a 500.
research_admin.changes: the 'status' query value is passed straight to Mongo. It is admin-only and a str, so the risk is low, but consider limiting it to an enum.
health(): the 'days' value returned in the response is the raw value, not the clamped one (e.g. days=999 reports 999 while the query uses 180).
ResearchHealthCard uses .catch(() => {}) everywhere, so errors are silently swallowed.
seed_data_creation: Inserted 2 TEST_ docs into legal_source_changes (one via pytest, one for the UI test). Both were deleted by _id. app_settings lex_ai_discovery was confirmed enabled=true at the end. Law monitoring was not toggled.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Admin UI: open /app, put aa_token, aa_terms='1', aa_cookie_consent='essential' and aa_welcomed='1' in localStorage, then click settings-btn. ResearchHealthCard sits under LawMonitoringCard. Run tests/test_research_admin_api.py with -p no:xdist -o addopts=''. It makes 4 paid /lex/chat calls (deselect TestChat to avoid the cost) and writes the chat outputs to research_chat_outputs.json.
rca of the issue: Flaky PL test: read() keeps one in-flight download per article key, but _pl_doc keeps no in-flight entry per law. Four refs to the same act start four PDF downloads and parses, limited by Semaphore(3). With REF_WAIT=2.5s the slower ones come back as pending/failed and are dropped. The test process never sets N._db, so it has no Mongo cache and always starts cold.
